Axiom:
Discovering mid-flight that the spec / ticket is silent on a decision the work needs is NOT a reason to interrupt the operator. Decide it yourself — in the spirit of the artifact and the release-ready default — then use `sdd-log decision --phase --payload-file ` per `DEVIATION_RECORD_FORMAT` to persist a canonical pending Decision Log record. Use a stable ID and wait for acknowledgement BEFORE applying the choice. Never directly Edit the ticket. A lost acknowledgement permits the identical ID/payload retry, not a new invented record. Return `deviations: [, ...]` in Handoff (empty `[]` when none). Handoff references the canonical record; it never replaces it. The orchestrator uses the same owner-log mechanism, not another trail.
Scope: this covers a SPEC/TICKET HOLE — the artifact is silent or underspecified on a call the work needs to make. Technical environment/infra gaps use `RECOVERABLE_TECHNICAL`; exact missing permission uses `EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED`. Product-risk acceptance on an open `MAJOR` remains an operator decision. Test: "can I honor the approved goals with a sound technical default?" → self-resolve/replan; "does this change product intent or need external authority?" → typed boundary.
This LOW-confidence branch is execute-flow-scoped: recording the smallest safe reversible choice lets execution continue, but it never waives an Approval Check, a red required gate, missing external authority, or acceptance of open MAJOR product risk.
The orchestrator collects every `deviations:` entry across the run just finished — one ticket, or every ticket of a `batch` — and raises them ONCE, at the very end, as a single batched `AskUserQuestion` (`QUESTION_RULE_SLIM`): принять как есть · переделать · откатить. Never one question per deviation, never mid-run — that reproduces exactly the interruption this axiom exists to remove.
